config.name: r3 - replication (confirmed / likely, with source project) and scaling (same country + sector), database only
config.description: Portfolio-level workflow that reads only the review database (no document access). Every validated approach carries its evidence passages, the explicit project references found when it was extracted, and its project's country, sector and approval date. (1) Rules scan the passages for replication language, P-codes and project names. (2) Approaches are matched semantically to EARLIER approaches of other projects. (3) One model call per approach judges, from the passages and the candidate list, whether the approach replicates an earlier project (CONFIRMED when the text says so and the source project is identifiable; LIKELY when the text only refers to earlier experience and a closely matching earlier approach exists in another country) and which candidates are the same approach. (4) SCALING is recorded when a verified same approach exists in an earlier project of the same country and the same sector. Each approach ends with two columns: replication (level + source project) and scaling (source project).

corpus.label: Build corpus
corpus.summary: Validated approaches with evidence passages, explicit references, country, sector, FY (database only)

cues.label: Find cues
cues.summary: Replication / scaling language, P-codes and project names in the evidence passages

match.label: Match earlier approaches
match.summary: Semantic similarity to approaches of earlier projects; top 5 candidates

judge.label: Judge replication & sameness
judge.summary: One call per approach: replication level + source project; which candidates are the same approach

classify.label: Two columns
classify.summary: replication = confirmed / likely (+ source project); scaling = same approach earlier in the same country and sector

summarize.label: Story tables
summarize.summary: By sector, region, country and fiscal year; confirmed vs likely

write.label: Write results
write.summary: result.json + CSVs; the two columns written back to the database
